paper_title: Knowing You Don't Know Learning When to Continue Search in Multi-round   RAG through Self-Practicing
caption: Ablation study on different Critic model choices. Both follow the SIM-RAG setting with GPT-4 as the Reasoner, but the blue bar uses learned Flan-T5-783M as a Critic, while the red bar uses GPT-4 as the Critic (a.k.a., self-critique).
model_annotation: The bar chart presents an ablation study comparing the performance of two Critic model choices—Flan-T5-783M (blue bars) and GPT-4 (red bars)—within the SIM-RAG framework, where GPT-4 serves as the Reasoner in both cases. The horizontal axis lists six evaluation metrics across two datasets (TriviaQA, HotPotQA, 2Wiki) and two scoring types (EM and F1), ordered as: TriviaQA (EM), HotPotQA (EM), 2Wiki (EM), TriviaQA (F1), HotPotQA (F1), and 2Wiki (F1). The vertical axis represents performance scores ranging from 25 to 85, with major gridlines at intervals of 10. For EM scores, Flan-T5-783M outperforms GPT-4 on TriviaQA (77.3 vs. 77.1) and 2Wiki (44.5 vs. 32.5), while GPT-4 performs worse on HotPotQA (31.9 vs. 37.0). For F1 scores, GPT-4 as Critic achieves the highest score on TriviaQA (83.8 vs. 82.8), while Flan-T5-783M leads on HotPotQA (49.7 vs. 43.3) and 2Wiki (53.3 vs. 38.1). The chart visually highlights that GPT-4 as Critic is more effective on TriviaQA F1, whereas Flan-T5-783M generally performs better on other metrics, especially 2Wiki and HotPotQA F1, suggesting model-specific strengths depending on the evaluation dimension.
